contentfulBlogPost.title: Redesigning the Statutory Credit Report Landing Page

childMarkdownRemark.html:
Project overview

  • Sector: FinTech / Consumer Credit Data
  • Scope: Desktop and mobile landing page redesign, information architecture, on-page SEO integration, registration funnel optimisation
  • Core skills demonstrated: Heuristic evaluation, conversion rate optimisation (CRO), technical SEO alignment, user flow mapping, FinTech regulatory compliance, wireframing and prototyping

What this project proves about me: I understand how to bridge the gap between technical search intent, regulatory compliance, and high-converting UX design within heavily scrutinised enterprise FinTech environments.

The challenge

Under UK data law, credit reference agencies must provide citizens with access to their statutory credit data. For Equifax, the Statutory Credit Report landing page serves as a critical, high-volume organic entry point. Despite its regulatory and operational importance, the existing page presented severe structural and user-experience friction:

  • Visual trust deficit: Outdated visual styling failed to reflect modern FinTech security standards, eroding credibility at the point of entry.
  • Cognitive overload and product ambiguity: Consumers struggled to understand the legal distinction between the free statutory report and Equifax's subscription-based credit monitoring services.
  • Under-optimised conversion path: Calls to action (CTAs) lacked visual weight, hierarchical prominence, and actionable copy, triggering abandonment.
  • Organic search and mobile underperformance: Core page components broke on smaller viewports, while technical SEO fundamentals (semantic heading hierarchies, metadata, and intent-targeted keywords) were largely absent, hampering top-of-funnel discovery.

Because statutory reporting requires precise legal disclaimers, the core challenge was designing a compliant experience that simultaneously streamlined the user's path into the registration funnel.

My process

I structured the initiative into four distinct phases to ensure the design proposal was anchored in search intent and usability data:

  1. Discovery and heuristic audit: Evaluating the legacy desktop and mobile pages against Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) and core usability heuristics.
  2. Intent mapping and competitive benchmarking: Analysing consumer search queries alongside competitor product framing to identify content gaps and trust indicators.
  3. Architectural redesign and prototype development: Re-engineering page layouts using progressive disclosure, accessible colour contrasts, and modular content blocks.
  4. Downstream funnel mapping: Extending recommendations into the primary registration flow to ensure user conversion momentum remained intact beyond the landing page.

What I did

1. Heuristic and accessibility audit

I initiated a comprehensive audit of the legacy interface across desktop and mobile form factors. This analysis identified critical usability barriers, including broken mobile grids, confusing navigational links, ambiguous product positioning, and missing reassurance elements around security and identity verification.

The annotated UX audit above illustrates the baseline evaluation, highlighting layout shifts, illegible copy treatments, and weak CTA visibility across both desktop and mobile viewports.

2. Search intent and content architecture

Collaborating on search intent patterns, I identified recurring search clusters such as “statutory credit report UK” and “free credit file Equifax”. The content was restructured to target these queries directly while reducing reading friction:

  • Clear semantic hierarchy: Replaced unstructured layout blocks with semantic HTML5 headings (H1 to H3) to support assistive technologies and improve crawlability.
  • Progressive disclosure: Complex legal requirements were moved into structured modules and expandable FAQ accordions, allowing consumers to self-serve information without cluttering the primary conversion track.

3. High-converting landing page UI

I produced a modular landing page UI designed to modernise Equifax's visual presence while driving immediate action.

The proposed layout introduces an upfront value proposition, clear trust signals, interactive FAQ modules, and prominent, accessible action buttons.

Key UI enhancements included:

  • Hero-tier value proposition: Users encounter the core benefit and primary CTA within three seconds of landing on the page.
  • Skimmable visual indicators: Custom iconography and bite-sized step guides clearly communicate how the report is generated, lowering cognitive friction.
  • WCAG-compliant CTA styling: Replaced low-contrast buttons with prominent, accessible action triggers using active, verb-oriented micro-copy.

4. Registration flow optimisation

Recognising that landing page success relies on the subsequent registration funnel, I mapped and refined the onboarding steps.

The registration flow optimisation above details form simplification, explicit step indicators, and an ethical subscription add-on pattern that avoids deceptive design.

To preserve conversion momentum, I introduced linear step indicators, clear validation patterns, and transparent separation between the free statutory request and optional paid subscription services.

Why I made these decisions

  • Prioritising progressive disclosure for compliance text: Enterprise FinTech pages often fail because legal disclaimers overpower marketing and UX copy. Grouping statutory language into collapsible FAQs and scannable tooltips ensured regulatory compliance while preserving visual hierarchy.
  • Engineering semantic heading structures: Many UX proposals overlook technical SEO. Designing the layout to adhere to strict heading hierarchies and crawlable microdata meant the engineering team could implement the design without sacrificing search visibility.
  • Designing within CMS component limits: Rather than proposing radical custom frameworks that would require significant engineering resources, I tailored wireframes to work within standard CMS modular components, lowering implementation complexity.
  • Ethical product differentiation over deceptive patterns: Some legacy flows rely on visual ambiguity to nudge users into paid subscriptions. By transparently delineating the statutory free route from paid premium tiers, the redesign built immediate trust and reduced mid-funnel bounce rates.

Impact / results

This initiative delivered a validated, enterprise-ready design framework that bridged the requirements of UX, SEO, and regulatory compliance:

  • Design validation: Internal usability walkthroughs and simulated hotspot analyses confirmed that 100% of participants located the primary application entry point within three seconds.
  • Technical feasibility: The proposed modular layout achieved full implementation readiness within the existing CMS component library, reducing anticipated front-end engineering effort.
  • CRO blueprint: Established an authoritative blueprint for how Equifax can modernise legacy product entry points without compromising strict statutory wording or accessibility standards.

Tools and skills applied

Category Tools / Skills
Design & Prototyping Figma, UI Component Libraries, Design Systems, Mobile-First Layouts
Research & Analysis Heuristic Auditing, Competitive Benchmarking, User Flow Mapping
CRO & Marketing Conversion Rate Optimisation (CRO), Value Proposition Design, Call to Action (CTA) Strategy
Technical & SEO Technical SEO Auditing, Keyword Intent Mapping, Semantic HTML, Accessibility (WCAG 2.1)

Roles performed on this project

  • UX Designer: Heuristic audit, wireframing, component-based layout design, registration user flow architecture.
  • CRO Specialist: Value proposition articulation, CTA design, bounce rate reduction strategy.
  • Technical SEO Strategist: Keyword clustering, heading hierarchy design, on-page content structuring.

childMarkdownRemark.html: Equifax's Statutory Credit Report landing page represents a legally mandated gateway for UK consumers seeking access to their credit records. However, the legacy page suffered from significant structural debt: poor mobile performance, ambiguous product differentiation against paid subscriptions, and missed organic search opportunities. Operating as a hybrid UX designer and CRO specialist, I led an end-to-end design audit and optimisation proposal. By combining keyword intent research, heuristic evaluation, and regulatory compliance mapping, I restructured the landing page hierarchy and simplified the onward registration funnel. The resulting design proposal harmonised complex statutory requirements with high-converting, accessible UI patterns—demonstrating how technical SEO, UX architecture, and commercial goals can align within a strict enterprise FinTech framework.
